source.stem:
A ball is dropped from a table-top. Air resistance may be ignored.
Which row describes the velocity and the acceleration of the ball at point X?

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: N–N: attract; S–S: attract; N–S: attract.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: N–N: attract; S–S: attract; N–S: repel.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The compass needle stays pointing north instead of turning toward the South pole to its east.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Red N–red N: repel; red N–blue S: attract; red N–blue N: attract.

intelligence.enrichment: Unlike poles of two magnets attract each other, while like poles repel each other. A compass needle is also a magnet, so its North pole moves away from another North pole and moves towards a South pole. the pairing of pole names determines attraction or repulsion The learner predicts attraction for unlike poles and repulsion for like poles, including compass-needle cases. Any magnet pole should pull any other magnet pole because magnets are for attracting.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Exploring magnets. The student must decide: Predict whether two nearby magnetic poles will attract or repel.
